# Initial refine

## Pull Request by @tomusdrw

Related: #694 

This PR introduces initial version of refine. There is still many things to cross-check with the Gray Paper, but I think it's a solid base.

As part of the PR, I've made PVM-executor a separate package that is used both by `@typeberry/transition` (we could consider renaming to `@typeberry/on-chain`) and newly introduced `@typeberry/in-core`.

Refinement has two basic tests (to be expanded in the future) and is exposed via non-standard RPC method (`typeberry_refineWorkPackage`).

Unrelated (yet important) fixes:
- [x] `MAX_VALUE` constants were used incorrectly in some places (I32 vs U32 values).

Follow up tasks:
1. [ ] Implementation of `RefineExternalitiesImpl` (up for a better name here) - should be split into multiple PRs, especially the machine stuff.
2. [ ] GP cross-checking of refine checks
3. [ ] Work Packages Authorization
4. [ ] Fetch externalities implementation and refactor
5. [ ] D3L / audits encoding (erasure root, exported & imported segments, etc)

## Walkthrough

This PR introduces a new in-core work-package refinement engine with comprehensive supporting infrastructure. The main additions include: a new `InCore` class implementing work-package refinement with state validation and per-item processing, a `typeberry_refineWorkPackage` RPC handler with full validation schemas, two new packages (`@typeberry/executor` and `@typeberry/in-core`), enhanced `HandlerContext` with `pvmBackend` and `blake2b`, refactored `WorkExecResult` API using static factory methods, updated `PvmExecutor` with refine-path support, new `ReturnValue` and `ReturnStatus` types for host-call execution, and multiple constant exports and renames propagated throughout the codebase. Workspace organization has been updated to reflect the new packages.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~60 minutes

- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#878**: Implements full `InCore.refine` with Gray Paper cross-check requirements
- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#879**: Adds work-package authorization placeholder in the refine flow
- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#880**: Introduces `FetchExternalities.createForRefine` and Refine fetch context used by refine implementation
- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#877**: Implements stubbed `RefineExternalitiesImpl` methods targeting the same class

## Possibly related PRs

- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#770**: Sets `PvmBackend.Ananas` as default; this PR wires it into RPC and handlers
- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#829**: Modifies `WorkExecResult` construction/codec patterns similarly
- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#487**: Adds executor factory methods and in-core/refine execution plumbing alongside this PR
- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#873**: Refactors `ReturnValue`/`ReturnStatus` types in host-call execution surface

**Return typed errors instead of throwing; unhandled exceptions will crash refine rather than producing controlled PANIC.**

When any of these host call stubs are triggered (machineInit, machinePages, machinePeekFrom, etc.), throwing causes Promise rejection with no try-catch in the handler code. Handlers like `Machine`, `Pages`, and `Peek` await these calls without error wrapping, so unhandled rejections propagate up instead of allowing refine to deterministically fail via `Result.error(...)`.

Return `Result.error()` with the appropriate error variant for each method:
- `machinePages`: `Result.error(PagesError.NoMachine)` (or InvalidOperation/InvalidPage)
- `machineVoidPages`/`machineZeroPages`: `Result.error(ZeroVoidError.NoMachine)` (or InvalidPage)
- `machinePeekFrom`/`machinePokeInto`: `Result.error(PeekPokeError.NoMachine)` (or source/destination faults)
- `machineExpunge`/`machineInvoke`: `Result.error(NoMachineError)`
- `machineInit`: `Result.error(ProgramDecoderError)`
- `exportSegment`: `Result.error(SegmentExportError)`
- `historicalLookup`: return `null` (already correct return type)
